claims.claim: According to NOAA's May 2025 annual report, the 2024 global average surface temperature was 1.46 °C above the pre-industrial average.

citations.quote: The global average surface temperature was 2.32 Fahrenheit (1.29 degrees Celsius) above the 20th-century average (57.0 degrees Fahrenheit, or 13.9 degrees Celsius) and 2.63 degrees Fahrenheit (1.46 degrees Celsius) above the pre-industrial average (56.7 degrees Fahrenheit, or 13.7 degrees Celsius),
citations.note: partly supported: Passages confirm 1.46°C figure but omit May 2025 report date.

claims.claim: The WMO's January 2025 consolidated analysis put it at about 1.55 °C, with a margin of uncertainty of ±0.13 °C.

citations.quote: The global average surface temperature was 1.55 °C (with a margin of uncertainty of ± 0.13 °C) above the 1850-1900 average, according to WMO’s consolidated analysis of the six datasets.
citations.note: partly supported: Passages lack January 2025 but confirm 1.55°C ±0.13.

claims.claim: Copernicus's ERA5 data placed 2024 at 1.60 °C above an estimate of the pre-industrial level.

citations.quote: This is equivalent to 1.60°C above an estimate of the 1850-1900 temperature designated to be the pre-industrial level.
citations.note: partly supported: Passage explicitly states ERA5 and the 1.60°C figure.
